reviewMode: Adversarial. Refute, do not confirm. Every cited digest recomputed from live bytes and resolved by content hash rather than by trusting the subject's path labels. Every recited structure re-derived from its primary source rather than read back from the subject. Because this is a turn-2 repair of my own turn-1 MUST-FIX, I attacked the repair harder than a fresh claim: I tested whether it is complete on both surfaces my own requiredRemedy named, whether it overshoots into restating advisories as findings, and whether anything unrelated was smuggled in alongside it. I also diffed turn 1 against turn 2 so that every byte of change had to justify itself.
decisionRule: CONSENT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. I ran the twelve enumerated dispatch attacks and eleven independent attacks beyond dispatch. None landed. The verdict is CONSENT.
decision: CONSENT. The turn-2 draft lands D245-M1 and CODEX-D245-SF1 as one class, on both surfaces and in the established form, without restating the advisories as findings, without disturbing the ACCEPT 0/0 recitation, and without inventing a Codex identifier or a both-reviewers preservation claim. All seventeen cited digests reproduce from live bytes. The subject is unmoved at 0444.

observationsNotFindings.observation: The turn-1 draft and both turn-1 verdicts live on disk under un-suffixed names (coordinator-decisions.D-245.draft.md and coordinator-decisions.D-245.review-adversarial.*.json) while the turn-2 subject uses a .turn2. infix. The subject's three new Measured-inputs rows label them by role rather than by path, so nothing is misstated and every digest resolves; but a reader reconstructing custody from path labels alone would not find a .turn1. file. This is a naming convention of the artifact directory, not a defect in the entry, and I resolved all three by content hash.

The Stage A disposition table now mixes two kinds of residue under one '(no change requested)' title, with the advisory rows carrying their forward routing inside the Standing cell. That is accurate and it is the form both turn-1 remedies asked for. A later entry of this class could instead give advisories their own titled block, which would make the 'no change requested now, honesty work later' distinction legible without reading the cell. Presentation only; nothing turns on it.

Corpus v7's appliesFindingsOf records for v6 that Codex returned REJECT 0/1 on G21FXV6-S1 and that v6 was 'Not Dual REJECT. Not Dual ACCEPT.' The D-245 entry records only the v7 dual ACCEPT 0/0 and marks v3 through v6 as split predecessors, which is correct and is what the dispatch requires. I note it because a reader of the adopted entry alone will not see that the v6 split was a single-reviewer rejection; that history lives in the corpus bytes the entry pins, which is an acceptable place for it.
